questions.question: What does API stand for?

explanation.correct: API stands for Application Programming Interface — a set of rules allowing software applications to communicate with each other.
explanation.why: A, C, and D are not valid AWS or industry terms.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is used to CREATE a new resource?

explanation.correct: POST is used to create new data. Example: POST /orders creates a new order.
explanation.why: GET reads, PUT updates/replaces, DELETE removes. POST creates.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is used to READ data without modifying it?

explanation.correct: GET retrieves data without making any changes. It is safe and idempotent — calling it multiple times has no side effects.
explanation.why: POST creates, PUT updates, PATCH partially updates. Only GET is purely read-only.

questions.question: What is Amazon API Gateway?

options.text: A database service for storing API responses
A fully managed service for creating, publishing, and securing APIs
A networking service for connecting VPCs
A monitoring service for Lambda functions

explanation.correct: API Gateway is a fully managed service that acts as the front door for backend services — handling routing, auth, throttling, monitoring, and more.
explanation.why: A is DynamoDB/ElastiCache. C is VPC Peering/Transit Gateway. D is CloudWatch.

questions.question: What is a 'resource' in API Gateway?

options.text: An IAM role attached to API Gateway
A URL path that represents a logical entity in your API
A Lambda function connected to the API
An S3 bucket storing API responses

explanation.correct: A resource is a URL path like /orders or /users that represents an entity in your API. Resources form a tree starting from root /.
explanation.why: Resources are URL paths, not IAM roles, Lambda functions, or storage buckets.

questions.question: What is a 'method' in API Gateway?

options.text: The programming language used to write Lambda code
An HTTP verb (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) attached to a resource
The deployment stage of the API
The integration type used for routing

explanation.correct: A method is an HTTP verb attached to a resource defining what action clients can perform — e.g., GET /orders retrieves orders, POST /orders creates one.
explanation.why: Methods are HTTP verbs, not programming languages, stages, or integration types.

questions.question: What must you do after making changes to API Gateway resources or methods for clients to see those changes?

options.text: Deploy the API to a stage

explanation.correct: Changes to resources, methods, and integrations in API Gateway are NOT live until you explicitly deploy the API to a stage. This is the most common beginner mistake.
explanation.why: Lambda restarts, deleting the API, and IAM role changes don't affect deployment. You must use Actions → Deploy API.

questions.question: What is a 'stage' in API Gateway?

options.text: A named environment like dev, staging, or prod with its own invoke URL
An IAM policy attached to the API
A CloudWatch log group for the API

explanation.correct: A stage is a named reference to a deployment — representing an environment. Each stage gets its own URL: https://abc.execute-api.region.amazonaws.com/dev/orders vs /prod/orders.
explanation.why: Stages are environments, not Lambda versions, IAM policies, or log groups.

questions.question: What causes a CORS error when a browser-based frontend calls your API Gateway?

options.text: The Lambda function is returning an error
The API Gateway endpoint is private
The browser blocks cross-origin requests when CORS headers are not present

explanation.correct: Browsers enforce the Same-Origin Policy and block JavaScript requests to different domains unless the server includes CORS headers. API Gateway must have CORS enabled on the resource.
explanation.why: Lambda errors show in the response body. Private APIs cause connection failure, not CORS errors. Missing API keys return 403, not CORS errors.

questions.question: What is Lambda Proxy Integration in API Gateway?

options.text: API Gateway caches Lambda responses for faster access
API Gateway passes the full HTTP request as a JSON event to Lambda, and Lambda returns statusCode, headers, and body
Lambda directly calls API Gateway without going through the internet
Multiple Lambda functions share a single integration

explanation.correct: With Lambda Proxy Integration, API Gateway forwards the entire request (method, path, headers, query params, body) as a JSON event. Lambda must return an object with statusCode, headers, and body.
explanation.why: This is the recommended integration type — no mapping templates needed, Lambda controls the full response.

questions.question: What is the maximum execution timeout for an AWS Lambda function?

explanation.correct: Lambda's maximum execution timeout is 15 minutes (900 seconds). This is a hard limit — for longer-running tasks, use Step Functions, ECS, or EC2.
explanation.why: 1 minute and 5 minutes are too short. 1 hour exceeds Lambda's hard limit.

questions.question: What HTTP status code does API Gateway return when throttling limits are exceeded?

explanation.correct: When the request rate exceeds configured throttle limits, API Gateway returns 429 Too Many Requests. Clients should implement retry logic with exponential backoff.
explanation.why: 400 is a bad request format. 403 is authorization failure. 503 is service unavailable. 429 is specifically the rate limit response.

questions.question: Which API Gateway type supports API Keys and Usage Plans?

options.text: Both REST API and HTTP API

explanation.correct: API Keys and Usage Plans are a feature of REST API only. HTTP API does not support usage plans, making it unsuitable for APIs that need per-client rate limiting or quota management.
explanation.why: This is a common exam trap — HTTP API is cheaper but lacks several enterprise features including usage plans.

questions.question: What is the maximum response cache TTL for API Gateway?

explanation.correct: The maximum TTL for API Gateway's response cache is 3,600 seconds (1 hour). Default TTL is 300 seconds. Caching is only available on REST API, not HTTP API.
explanation.why: Memorize this number — it appears directly in exam questions about API Gateway caching.

questions.question: What is the default account-level throttle limit for API Gateway?

explanation.correct: The default throttle limit is 10,000 requests per second (steady state) with a burst limit of 5,000 requests. This is a soft limit that can be increased via AWS Support.
explanation.why: Both numbers matter for exam questions — know that steady rate is 10,000 and burst is 5,000.

questions.question: A developer needs custom authentication logic that checks a proprietary token format against a database. Which API Gateway authorizer should they use?

explanation.correct: Lambda Authorizer (Custom Authorizer) lets you write a Lambda function with any authentication logic — checking custom tokens, querying databases, integrating with legacy systems. It returns an IAM policy: allow or deny.
explanation.why: Cognito is for standard JWT from Cognito User Pools. API Keys are for developer/partner access. IAM auth requires AWS SigV4 signing.

questions.question: Which authorizer is best for a mobile app where end users log in and the API needs to validate their JWT tokens?

explanation.correct: Cognito Authorizer is designed for user-facing applications. Users log in via Cognito User Pools, receive a JWT token, include it in API calls, and API Gateway validates it automatically.
explanation.why: API Keys are for developer/partner access, not end users. Lambda Authorizer is for custom logic. Cognito is the managed solution for user authentication.

questions.question: What does enabling CORS on an API Gateway resource automatically create?

options.text: A new Lambda function to handle CORS
An OPTIONS method that responds to browser preflight requests
An IAM role allowing cross-account access
A new stage for cross-origin deployments

explanation.correct: CORS enabling automatically creates an OPTIONS method on the resource. Browsers send an OPTIONS preflight request before cross-origin POST/PUT calls to verify the server allows them.
explanation.why: CORS is handled by HTTP headers and methods, not Lambda functions, IAM roles, or stages.

questions.question: Which AWS service can you associate with API Gateway REST API to protect against SQL injection and XSS attacks?

explanation.correct: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) can be associated with API Gateway REST API to filter out common web exploits like SQL injection, XSS, and rate-based attack patterns before they reach your backend.
explanation.why: Shield protects against DDoS at network layer. Inspector scans EC2/containers for vulnerabilities. GuardDuty is threat detection using logs.

questions.question: What is the key difference between REST API and HTTP API in terms of cost?

options.text: REST API is free, HTTP API has charges
HTTP API is approximately 70% cheaper than REST API
HTTP API charges per connection, REST API per request

explanation.correct: HTTP API is approximately 70% cheaper than REST API (roughly $1/million requests vs $3.50/million). The tradeoff is that HTTP API lacks advanced features like usage plans, caching, WAF, and request validation.
explanation.why: Neither is free beyond the free tier. The 70% cost savings for HTTP API is a commonly tested fact.

questions.question: Stage variables in API Gateway are commonly used to do what?

options.text: Point different stages to different Lambda function versions or aliases
Define CORS allowed origins per stage

explanation.correct: Stage variables are key-value pairs at the stage level. A common pattern is setting lambdaAlias=prod for the prod stage and lambdaAlias=dev for the dev stage, then using ${stageVariables.lambdaAlias} in the Lambda function name field.
explanation.why: This allows the same API definition to route to different Lambda code per environment without changing the API structure.

questions.question: A private API Gateway can only be accessed from where?

options.text: Only from the same AWS region
Only from IAM users in the same account
Only from within a VPC via a VPC Interface Endpoint

explanation.correct: A Private API endpoint is only reachable from within a VPC through a VPC Interface Endpoint (powered by AWS PrivateLink). It cannot be accessed from the public internet regardless of any other configuration.
explanation.why: This is the combination from the VPC Endpoints notes — Private API + Interface Endpoint = VPC-only access. Not region-based, IAM-based, or Direct Connect-specific.

questions.question: Your API Gateway is receiving 15,000 requests/second. The default account limit is 10,000 RPS. What happens to the excess 5,000 requests?

options.text: They are queued and processed when capacity is available
They are rejected with 429 Too Many Requests
They are routed to a backup Lambda function
API Gateway automatically scales to handle all requests

explanation.correct: API Gateway does not queue excess requests. Any request exceeding the throttle limit is immediately rejected with 429 Too Many Requests. Clients must implement retry logic with exponential backoff.
explanation.why: This is an important architectural point — API Gateway fails fast, it doesn't buffer. Design your clients to handle 429 responses.

questions.question: Which combination forms a complete serverless application stack with no servers to manage?

explanation.correct: API Gateway (managed HTTP routing) + Lambda (managed compute) + DynamoDB (managed NoSQL database) = fully serverless stack. No EC2 instances, no server management, pay only for actual usage.
explanation.why: EC2 and RDS require server management. ALB + Lambda is partially serverless but ALB isn't the API management layer. CloudFront + EC2 involves servers.

questions.question: Why doesn't API Gateway response caching apply to POST requests?

options.text: POST requests are too large to cache
POST requests modify data, so returning a cached response could serve stale data or skip important write operations
POST requests don't have a URL to use as a cache key
AWS decided POST caching would be too expensive

explanation.correct: POST requests create or modify data. Caching a POST response would mean the creation operation might not execute (because the cache serves the old response), leading to missed writes and stale data. Only idempotent read operations (GET) should be cached.
explanation.why: This is a fundamental RESTful API design principle, not a technical limitation of URL length or cost.

questions.question: A Lambda Authorizer returns an IAM policy to API Gateway. If the policy says DENY, what does API Gateway do?

options.text: Calls the Lambda function anyway but logs the denial
Returns 403 Forbidden to the client without calling the backend Lambda
Returns 401 Unauthorized and asks the client to re-authenticate
Routes the request to a different Lambda function

explanation.correct: When a Lambda Authorizer returns a DENY policy, API Gateway immediately returns 403 Forbidden to the client. The backend Lambda (integration) never executes. This is the security gate pattern.
explanation.why: This is why authorizers are valuable — they protect backend resources from unauthorized calls without running expensive Lambda functions.

questions.question: You need to support 3 partner companies with different API rate limits without writing any code changes. What combination do you configure?

options.text: Three API Keys, each associated with a different Usage Plan
Three CloudWatch alarms with throttle rules

explanation.correct: Create one API key per partner. Create one usage plan per tier (or per partner) with the desired rate/quota limits. Associate each API key with its usage plan. API Gateway enforces the limits automatically per key.
explanation.why: Three separate APIs is operationally expensive. Lambda Authorizers don't enforce rate limits. CloudWatch alarms are for alerting, not rate limiting.

questions.question: When would you choose an ALB (Application Load Balancer) over API Gateway?

options.text: When you need API key management and usage plans
When you need to distribute traffic across multiple EC2 instances with health checks

explanation.correct: ALB is the right choice when you need to load balance traffic across a fleet of EC2 instances or containers with health checks and sticky sessions. API Gateway is for API management; ALB is for traffic distribution.
explanation.why: API key management, caching, and WAF are API Gateway features. ALB doesn't have these. ALB excels at load balancing HTTP traffic to multiple backends.

questions.question: What happens to a Lambda function when 500 users simultaneously call an API endpoint?

options.text: Lambda queues all 500 requests and processes them one at a time
Only one Lambda execution runs and serves all 500 users
API Gateway automatically rejects requests above the Lambda concurrency limit

explanation.correct: Lambda creates one independent execution per simultaneous invocation. 500 concurrent users = 500 parallel Lambda executions. Each runs independently in its own container. This auto-scaling behavior is what makes Lambda suitable for unpredictable traffic.
explanation.why: Lambda does not queue requests or reuse executions for different callers. The default concurrency limit is 1,000 per region — above that, requests are throttled.

questions.question: A REST API is deployed. A developer updates a method's Lambda integration to point to a new Lambda function. Will existing callers immediately see responses from the new Lambda?

options.text: Yes, changes to integrations are live immediately
No, the API must be redeployed to the stage for the change to take effect
Yes, but only after the old Lambda's cache TTL expires
No, a new API must be created with the new Lambda

explanation.correct: Any change to API Gateway — resources, methods, integrations, authorizers, models — requires a new deployment to a stage before the change affects live callers. This is a deliberate design that prevents accidental live changes.
explanation.why: This is one of the most tested and most commonly encountered real-world gotchas with API Gateway. Always redeploy after making changes.
